claim_verdicts.evidence: index.md:14: "EF Core compares the current model against a snapshot of the old model to determine the differences, and generates migration source files; the files can be tracked in your project's source control like any other source file." index.md:114: "the model snapshot is one of the files generated by EF Core when you add a migration, and is checked into source control". index.md:70 + applying.md:156: `dotnet ef database update` "updates your database to the latest migration". The diff base is the snapshot file (DonHangDbContextModelSnapshot.cs at stage-1), not "the last migration".
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: `dotnet ef migrations add <Name>` compares the current model against a snapshot of the model as it was at the last migration (a file EF Core writes under `Migrations/`) and writes the difference as a new migration file; `dotnet ef database update` applies to a database every migration it has not recorded yet.

claim_verdicts.evidence: applying.md:399 ("Apply migrations at runtime"): "It's possible for the application itself to apply migrations programmatically, typically during startup." Same section: "To apply migrations programmatically, call `context.Database.MigrateAsync()`" with an ASP.NET sample calling it once in a service scope after Build(). applying.md:340: "As with `dotnet ef database update` or `Update-Database`, migrations are applied to the database only if they have not been already applied." Program.cs at stage-1 calls the sync `context.Database.Migrate()` once inside such a scope.

history-table.md:11: "By default, EF Core keeps track of which migrations have been applied to the database by recording them in a table named `__EFMigrationsHistory`." managing.md:332-336 ("Resetting all migrations"), step 5: "Insert a single row into the migrations history, to record that the first migration has already been applied, since your tables are already there", with `INSERT INTO [__EFMigrationsHistory] ([MIGRATIONID], [PRODUCTVERSION]) VALUES (...)`. Note the docs say "by default"; the lesson states the name unconditionally.

MigrationBaseline.cs:22-40 at stage-1: returns when to_regclass('public."__EFMigrationsHistory"') is not DBNull; returns when to_regclass('public.customers') is DBNull; otherwise runs CommandText = 'CREATE TABLE "__EFMigrationsHistory" ("MigrationId" character varying(150) NOT NULL, "ProductVersion" character varying(32) NOT NULL, CONSTRAINT "PK___EFMigrationsHistory" PRIMARY KEY ("MigrationId")); INSERT INTO ... VALUES (''20260923154631_InitialCreate'', ''10.0.4'');'. The claim and the lesson omit that it CREATEs the table first.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: MigrationBaseline.ApplyIfNeeded returns early if __EFMigrationsHistory exists, or if customers does not; otherwise it creates the __EFMigrationsHistory table itself (MigrationId varchar(150) PK, ProductVersion varchar(32)) and inserts one row for 20260923154631_InitialCreate / 10.0.4, then returns without running any migration.

claim_verdicts.evidence: Program.cs at stage-1, lines 52-62: `var app = builder.Build();` then `using (var scope = app.Services.CreateScope()) { var context = scope.ServiceProvider.GetRequiredService<DonHangDbContext>(); MigrationBaseline.ApplyIfNeeded(context); context.Database.Migrate(); }` — and only after that block `app.UseMiddleware<ExceptionHandlingMiddleware>(); app.UseMiddleware<RequestLoggingMiddleware>(); app.UseCors(); app.UseAuthentication();`. Exactly one call, immediately before Migrate(), before any middleware.

20260923154700_AddPasswordHashToCustomers.cs:13-35 at stage-1: Up calls AddColumn<string>(name: "password_hash", table: "customers", type: "text", nullable: true), then migrationBuilder.Sql("UPDATE customers SET password_hash = '100000...' WHERE id IN (1, 2, 3, 4, 5);"); Down calls DropColumn(name: "password_hash", table: "customers"). Live lab confirms the 5 rows: `select count(*), count(password_hash) from customers` -> 5 | 5.

Live run this session: `docker exec donhang-db psql -U donhang -d donhang -c 'select "MigrationId","ProductVersion" from "__EFMigrationsHistory" order by "MigrationId";'` -> 20260923154631_InitialCreate | 10.0.4; 20260923154700_AddPasswordHashToCustomers | 10.0.4; 20260924092625_AddOrderCustomerNavigation | 10.0.4; (3 rows). `git ls-tree -r stage-1 -- DonHang.Infrastructure/Migrations/` lists 7 files: those 3 .cs, their 3 .Designer.cs, and DonHangDbContextModelSnapshot.cs.

issues.text: The prose about MigrationBaseline says it only inserts a row, but the code block shown two paragraphs later creates the table first: `CREATE TABLE "__EFMigrationsHistory" (...)` then `INSERT INTO`. As written the mechanism is incoherent — the paragraph states there is no history table yet, then has the code insert into it. The mermaid edge `E -.->|MigrationBaseline inserts InitialCreate's row| D` has the same omission.
issues.fix: In 'How it works': "...and, instead of letting `InitialCreate` run, creates `__EFMigrationsHistory` itself with the two columns EF Core uses and inserts one row recording `InitialCreate` as already applied." Change the mermaid label to `MigrationBaseline creates the table + InitialCreate's row`. Update claim 4 in .meta.json to match.
issues.quote: instead of letting `InitialCreate` run, inserts one row into `__EFMigrationsHistory` recording it as already applied

issues.text: Unlisted claim, and too strong: "not one you write by hand" is contradicted by the docs (index.md:61 "It's a good idea to inspect what exactly EF Core generated - and possibly amend it"; managing.md has a 'Customize migration code' section) and by this lesson's own section 5: "the `migrationBuilder.Sql(...)` backfill is the one part a person added afterward". issues.text: Unlisted claim: a behaviour statement about what Migrate() would do on a schema.sql-built database is nowhere in `claims`. It is true — InitialCreate.cs:15-92 calls CreateTable for customers/notifications/orders/payments/products/order_items, and `CREATE TABLE customers (id integer);` on the running lab DB returns `ERROR: relation "customers" already exists` — but the author must own it, since the whole lesson turns on it.
issues.fix: Add to .meta.json `claims` a claim of kind `behavior`, section 4: "Migrate() on a database whose tables came from db/schema.sql but whose history table is empty runs InitialCreate's CreateTable calls and fails with 'relation already exists'", source_hint: InitialCreate.cs:15-92 + psql run + managing.md 'Resetting all migrations' step 5.
issues.quote: If `Migrate()` saw an empty history table, it would try to run `InitialCreate`'s table-creation calls against tables that already exist, and fail.

issues.text: Unlisted claim stated as a universal fact about process: whether a schema change is reviewed depends on the team, not on EF Core. The docs support only the weaker form — index.md:14 "the files can be tracked in your project's source control like any other source file", applying.md:35 "SQL scripts can be reviewed for accuracy; this is important since applying schema changes to production databases is a potentially dangerous operation". Repeated verbatim in the five-line summary, line 5.
issues.fix: Soften both places to the conditional form: "...a schema change can go through the same code review as any other file in source control — a reviewer can read the exact `AddColumn`/`Sql` calls before they ever reach a database." Register it in `claims` with source index.md:14.
issues.quote: a schema change goes through code review the same way any other code change does

issues.text: Ambiguous stem. "what happens when Đơn Hàng's API starts" is only true of the first start against a schema.sql-built database: on every later start ApplyIfNeeded returns at its first check (history table exists) and no migration runs — while the lesson says Migrate() runs "every time the API process starts".
